sentences.text: Ajay Majhi vs Unknown on 24 December, 2025

rrc Calcutta High Court In the Circuit Bench at Jalpaiguri Appellate Side Crm (A) 954 of
2025 Re: An application for anticipatory bail under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita, 2023. In the matter of : Ajay Majhi ..... petitioner Mr. Pratap Khati Mr. Nishant Nav Rasaily

..... For the petitioner Mr. Abhijit Sarkar Mr. Bhaskar Das .....For the State Apprehending arrest in connection with Bagdogra Police Station Case No. 207 of 2025 dated 19.06.2025 under Section 69 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (corresponding to Section 376 IPC), the present application has been preferred.

entities.text: Bagdogra Police Station Case No. 207 of 2025
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Mr. Khati, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that both the petitioner and the de facto complainant are adults.
There was a love relationship between them for about a period of 8 years.
Thereafter, the complaint was lodged by the de facto complainant falsely implicating the petitioner by giving an exaggerated account.
In the said conspectus, the petitioner may be granted anticipatory bail.
Reliance has been placed upon an unreported judgment delivered in the case of Bhawar Singh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh.

entities.text: Bhawar Singh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Sarkar, learned advocate appearing for the State opposes the petitioner's prayer and submits that there are strong incriminating materials on record against the petitioner and the petitioner's implication cannot be totally ruled out at this stage, moreso when investigation is still continuing.

Prima facie, whether free-mixing among the petitioner and the de facto complainant for about a period of 8 years prior to the incident was actuate with dishonest intention or deception, is to be assessed at the appropriate stage of the proceedings, in accordance with law.
Considering the nature of accusations and the extent of complicity of the petitioner in the alleged offence, I am of the opinion that his custodial interrogation is not necessary.
However, his movement needs to be restricted.

In view thereof, we allow this application and direct that in the event of arrest the petitioner,
namely, Ajay Majhi shall be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/-, with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 482(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 with a further condition that the petitioner shall meet with the investigation officer of the case once a week till investigation is complete.

In the event the petitioner fails to comply with the aforesaid directions, without any justifiable cause, the learned Court below shall be at liberty to cancel his bail, without any further reference to this Court.
The application for anticipatory bail, being CRM (A) 954 of 2025, is, thus, disposed of.
